name: Cook & Persinger 1997: Thomas pattern at four repeat intervals (29 min)
summary: The Thomas-pattern part of Cook & Persinger 1997: the 849-point pattern at 1-ms points in four 5-min presentations with 3 min without field between them; the pause between patterns is 3, 33, 330 and 3000 ms in turn. The paper reports that the 330 ms interval was the only one that predicted the number of button presses for a sensed presence.
notes: Cook & Persinger presented the Thomas pulse at 1-ms points four times, 5 min each, with 3 min of no field between, and with 3, 33, 330 and 3000 ms between patterns (Cook 1997 pp.4-5 [686-687]). It was given to one exceptional subject and in Exp. III. This program plays the four blocks in that order with the 849-point table of US 6,234,953 (Table 1); the paper also gives 849 points (p.4 [686]). The table matches the description in Buckner 2015 p.2 (18 doublets); it was not compared point for point with the lab's file. The lab's computer added 0.19 ms to each point (p.4 [686]); this helmet plays 1.0 ms. In every block one left-right pair is on at a time, and the right side is reversed so that the pair's field points through the head. Each pair stays on for 0.5 s. The four sites per side stand for the lab helmet's four solenoids per side on a 7.5 by 5 cm ellipse; the site names are this project's reading. Field: the paper gives 5 uT at 1 cm from the source and 1 uT within 4 cm (p.4 [686]). This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. At 1 uT this helmet gives about 4.4 uT at 10 mm and 0.18 uT at 40 mm. Support: one lab and small groups. The outcome was the number of button presses for a sensed presence, and the typical report during the Thomas pattern was of unpleasant vibrations through the body (p.7 [689]). Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). persinger-cook-1997-pattern-screen plays the paper's four-pattern sequence. Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history, implanted devices or pregnancy; stop at once on fear, headache or distress.
setting: Blindfolded, reclining in a quiet, dark room; a helper runs the program and records the clock time of each reported experience, without knowing or revealing which block is active.
